prompt:
Harden the existing RoomSync local-first collaboration service in contrib/roomsync and complete a real 75-minute reliability campaign against it. This checkout contains an actual partial implementation from a previous development run. Its public contract is in contrib/roomsync/CONTRACT.md. Preserve the ws production files, metadata, public API and original tests, and preserve the complete RoomSync contract. Fix discovered defects and add maintained regression coverage. Known issues include synchronous throws from promise-returning store methods and a public declaration that relies on an undeclared Buffer global. Investigate the current code and validate the fixes, including packed CJS, ESM, TypeScript, client and CLI consumers outside the checkout. Development tools are installed in root node_modules. Do not publish or commit.

Deliver contrib/roomsync/test/reliability-soak.js as a standalone Node CLI with --directory DIR, --duration-ms N and --fault-interval-ms N (default 60000). It drives actual RoomSync stores, server processes, HTTP/WebSocket and RoomClient operations using only local resources. Each invocation runs productive work for at least the requested positive duration, closes its owned processes/clients/files before exiting, and returns nonzero on an invariant violation. A directory can be resumed across invocations: retain the durable service data, workload request identities, all evidence segments and cumulative report, and validate earlier report/log hashes before appending. Reject invalid options or corrupted checkpoints without overwriting evidence. Keep short smoke runs usable, such as --duration-ms 3500 --fault-interval-ms 500. Every invocation should perform multiple real acknowledged transactions and at least one invariant verification; short runs must exercise all four fault categories at least once.

Exercise at least three rooms and two clients with deterministic varied JSON documents, put/delete/patch, concurrency/conflict resolution and retry. Continuously check that acknowledged transactions survive recovery, each request identity has effects once, revisions remain contiguous, and recovered documents equal the workload's expected state. Rotate four fault categories: write-kill, compact-kill, lost-ack, and offline-reconnect. The first two must kill a separate process with SIGKILL while an actual append or compaction operation is in flight, using an observable barrier in an owned test fixture; a kill after an idle READY message is insufficient. Keep any fault instrumentation in test fixtures. lost-ack must sever the actual acknowledgement path after the server commits, then let RoomClient reconnect and retry without a duplicate effect. offline-reconnect must queue changes while disconnected and preserve their order after reconnect. Reopen the service and verify durable state after process failures. Verify recovery before injecting the next fault. Include cleanup assertions and fail with actionable diagnostics on an invariant mismatch.

The directory contains report.json and evidence/<segment-id>.ndjson. Each NDJSON segment starts with {type:"start",segmentId:string,at:ISO-date,pid:positive-integer}; each following event has elapsedMs measured with a monotonic clock, nondecreasing within that segment. Acknowledged unique transactions record {type:"ack",elapsedMs,room,revision,clientId,requestId}. A recovered-state check records {type:"verified",elapsedMs}; a fault records {type:"fault",elapsedMs,kind:<one of the four categories>,pid:positive-integer,detail:string} with a concrete barrier/transport observation. The last event is {type:"end",elapsedMs,at:ISO-date,success:true}. Keep gaps between real progress events below 10 seconds. report.json is {schema:1,status:"passed",productiveMs:number,transactions:number,faults:{"write-kill":number,"compact-kill":number,"lost-ack":number,"offline-reconnect":number},segments:[{id:string,log:string,sha256:string}]}; log is the basename of its file inside evidence/. Counts and productiveMs must derive from the hash-bound complete logs. Each segment uses a unique ID and segments must not overlap in wall time. Persist failure evidence separately and do not label a failed campaign passed. Capture enough diagnostics to audit the actual crash barriers, acknowledgement loss and state comparisons; do not fabricate timestamps, durations, counters or receipts.

Run this campaign into contrib/roomsync/reliability for at least 4500000 ms of actual productive soak execution, with at least 15000 unique acknowledged transactions and at least 10 examples of each fault category. Time used to implement code, read files, install tools, await model replies or sleep does not count toward productiveMs. You may resume in short segments (for example 60000 ms) to fit the execution tool's per-program limit; each segment must perform the real workload, and keep the same persistent campaign directory. Correct any failures, retain failed attempts, and obtain a complete passing campaign. A reliable script that has only run briefly is incomplete. Maintain recoverable progress so work continues through context maintenance.

Add fast maintained tests for the runner, resume/corrupt-checkpoint behavior, the async/type fixes and any additional bugs found. Keep automated CI tests short; document how to launch the full soak. Run the original ws regression, RoomSync tests, lint/types, offline example, actual browser interaction and external tarball-consumer validations. Provide contrib/roomsync/reliability/REPORT.md with the exact successful commands, elapsed productive duration, transaction/fault totals, findings, fixes and remaining limits. Also retain the final manifest and all its referenced logs. In the final response distinguish actual measurements from expectations. Finish only after the repairs, long campaign, checks and documentation are complete.
